note: Lean assumes $g$ non-increasing (text: any $g$, with the running max) and gives the discrete sum, which equals the integral form for non-increasing $g$; it needs no sign on $f$, no regularity of $F$, and the partial-sum bound only at integers.

snippet.text:
/-- Abel summation, inequality form: if `g` is non-increasing and `≥ 0` on `[a, b]` and the
partial sums `S(n) = Σ_{a ≤ m ≤ n} f(m)` satisfy `S(n) ≤ F(n)`, then
`Σ_{a ≤ n ≤ b} f(n) g(n) ≤ g(a) F(a) + Σ_{a < n ≤ b} g(n)(F(n) − F(n−1))`. -/
theorem abel_le {f g F : ℕ → ℝ} {a b : ℕ} (hab : a ≤ b)
    (hg : ∀ n, a ≤ n → n < b → g (n + 1) ≤ g n) (hg0 : 0 ≤ g b)

proof_context.conclusion: For non-increasing $g\ge0$ at $b$ and partial sums $\sum_{a\le m\le n}f(m)\le F(n)$: $\sum_{a\le n\le b}f(n)g(n)\le g(a)F(a)+\sum_{a<n\le b}g(n)(F(n)-F(n-1))$.
